text: Question: The nurse is caring for a client who sustained a cervical spinal cord injury and had halo traction therapy applied 1 day ago.  Which of the following should the nurse include in the care plan?
A. Cleanse the halo traction pin sites with 100% hydrogen peroxide.
B. Maintain the client’s neck in a flexed position.
C. Expect drainage around the halo traction pins for the first 72 hours.
D. Change the client’s position via logroll.
Correct answer: D. Change the client’s position via logroll.
Topic: Neuro, Eyes & Ortho
notes: Rationale:
Weekly quiz key (one answer):
• Change the client’s position via logroll.
(This answer is keyed in the original quiz source.)
Study notes from your master guide (not official Galen rationales):
• “Change the client’s position via logroll.” – Logroll preserves spinal alignment
Not correct:
• “Cleanse the halo traction pin sites with 100% hydrogen peroxide.” – Full-strength peroxide damages tissue; follow pin-care protocol
• “Maintain the client’s neck in a flexed position.” – Maintain neutral alignment
• “Expect drainage around the halo traction pins for the first 72 hours.” – Drainage may indicate infection; assess rather than assume normal
Not covered in your class PowerPoints, so this answer comes from the quiz file only.

slides.title: A nurse is caring for the client who has Ménière's disease and asks if he is all
text: Question: A nurse is caring for the client who has Ménière's disease and asks if he is allowed to ambulate independently. Which of the following responses should the nurse make?
A. "Please ring for assistance when you wish to get out of bed."
B. "We will have to get a prescription from your provider."
C. "No, you are on strict bedrest and must not be up."
D. "Yes, you are free to move around as you wish."
Correct answer: A. "Please ring for assistance when you wish to get out of bed."
Topic: Neuro, Eyes & Ortho
notes: Rationale:
Weekly quiz key (one answer):
• "Please ring for assistance when you wish to get out of bed."
(This answer was inferred when the master guide was put together; it is not keyed in the original quiz source.)
Study notes from your master guide (not official Galen rationales):
• “"Please ring for assistance when you wish to get out of bed."” – Vertigo increases fall risk
Not correct:
• “"We will have to get a prescription from your provider."” – Nursing safety assistance does not require a prescription
• “"No, you are on strict bedrest and must not be up."” – Strict bedrest not routinely required
• “"Yes, you are free to move around as you wish."” – Unassisted mobility risks falls

slides.title: The nurse has given medication instructions to a patient receiving phenytoin. Wh
text: Question: The nurse has given medication instructions to a patient receiving phenytoin. Which statement by the patient indicates that the patient has an adequate understanding?
A. “I can skip doses if the side effects bother me.”
B. “I will need to take extra care of my teeth and gums while on this medication.”
C. “I can go out for a beer while on this medication.”
D. “I will be able to stop taking this drug once the seizures stop.”
Correct answer: B. “I will need to take extra care of my teeth and gums while on this medication.”
Topic: Neuro, Eyes & Ortho
notes: Rationale:
Weekly quiz key (one answer):
• “I will need to take extra care of my teeth and gums while on this medication.”
(This answer is keyed in the original quiz source.)
Study notes from your master guide (not official Galen rationales):
• ““I will need to take extra care of my teeth and gums while on this medication.”” – Phenytoin may cause gingival overgrowth
Not correct:
• ““I can skip doses if the side effects bother me.”” – Abrupt interruption risks seizures
• ““I can go out for a beer while on this medication.”” – Alcohol may interact or impair safety
• ““I will be able to stop taking this drug once the seizures stop.”” – Do not stop without provider-directed taper

text: Question: During the taking of the health history of a 78-year-old man, his wife states that he occasionally has problems with short-term memory loss and confusion: “He can’t even remember how to button his shirt.” When assessing his sensory system, which action by the nurse is most appropriate?
A. The nurse would perform the tests, knowing that mental status does not affect sensory ability.
B. Before testing, the nurse would assess the patient’s mental status and ability to follow directions.
C. The nurse would not test the sensory system as part of the examination because the results would not be valid.
D. The nurse would proceed with an explanation of each test, making certain that the wife understands.
Correct answer: B. Before testing, the nurse would assess the patient’s mental status and ability to follow directions.
Topic: Neuro, Eyes & Ortho
notes: Rationale:
Weekly quiz key (one answer):
• Before testing, the nurse would assess the patient’s mental status and ability to follow directions.
(This answer is keyed in the original quiz source.)
Study notes from your master guide (not official Galen rationales):
• “Before testing, the nurse would assess the patient’s mental status and ability to follo…” – Check ability to understand and follow commands
Not correct:
• “The nurse would perform the tests, knowing that mental status does not affect sensory a…” – Cognitive status affects test reliability
• “The nurse would not test the sensory system as part of the examination because the resu…” – Do not automatically omit testing
• “The nurse would proceed with an explanation of each test, making certain that the wife …” – Patient participation matters more than wife understanding

slides.title: A 21-year-old patient has a head injury resulting from trauma and is unconscious
text: Question: A 21-year-old patient has a head injury resulting from trauma and is unconscious. There are no other injuries. During the assessment what would the nurse expect to find when testing the patient’s deep tendon reflexes?
A. Reflexes cannot be elicited.
B. All reflexes will be diminished but present.
C. Some reflexes will be present, depending on the area of injury.
D. Reflexes will be normal.
Correct answer: D. Reflexes will be normal.
Topic: Burns, Trauma & Emergencies
notes: Rationale:
Weekly quiz key (one answer):
• Reflexes will be normal.
(This answer is keyed in the original quiz source.)
Study notes from your master guide (not official Galen rationales):
• “Reflexes will be normal.” – Source assumption of intact reflex arcs; actual findings vary
Not correct:
• “Reflexes cannot be elicited.” – Unconsciousness alone does not abolish reflexes
• “All reflexes will be diminished but present.” – Reduced reflexes are not inevitable
• “Some reflexes will be present, depending on the area of injury.” – Clinically possible depending on injury; source expects D

slides.title: The client has Guillain-Barré syndrome. Which interdisciplinary health care team
text: Question: The client has Guillain-Barré syndrome. Which interdisciplinary health care team members will the nurse plan to collaborate with to help prevent pressure ulcers related to immobility in the client with Guillain-Barré syndrome? Select all that apply.
A. Social worker
B. Occupational therapist (OT)
C. Family
D. Dietitian
E. Certified hospital chaplain
Correct answers: B. Occupational therapist (OT); C. Family; D. Dietitian
Topic: GI & Nutrition
notes: Rationale:
Weekly quiz key (select all):
• Occupational therapist (OT)
• Family
• Dietitian
(This answer was inferred when the master guide was put together; it is not keyed in the original quiz source.)
Study notes from your master guide (not official Galen rationales):
• “Occupational therapist (OT)” – Supports positioning and adaptive equipment
• “Family” – Can assist with turning and skin inspection
• “Dietitian” – Supports adequate nutrition for skin integrity
Not correct:
• “Social worker” – Addresses resources, not direct pressure prevention in this item
• “Certified hospital chaplain” – Spiritual care not direct pressure prevention

slides.title: An 80-year-old client is bedridden after having a cerebrovascular accident (CVA)
text: Question: An 80-year-old client is bedridden after having a cerebrovascular accident (CVA). Which nursing intervention is used to help prevent skin breakdown?
A. Applying moist packs to the skin every shift
B. Turning and repositioning at least every 4 hours
C. Assuring the client's skin remains dry and clean.
D. Decreasing calories consumed; avoiding weight gain
Correct answer: C. Assuring the client's skin remains dry and clean.
Topic: Cardiovascular
notes: Rationale:
Weekly quiz key (one answer):
• Assuring the client's skin remains dry and clean.
(This answer was inferred when the master guide was put together; it is not keyed in the original quiz source.)
Study notes from your master guide (not official Galen rationales):
• “Assuring the client's skin remains dry and clean.” – Clean dry skin reduces moisture injury
Not correct:
• “Applying moist packs to the skin every shift” – Excess moisture promotes skin breakdown
• “Turning and repositioning at least every 4 hours” – Four hours may be too long for some patients
• “Decreasing calories consumed; avoiding weight gain” – Adequate calories and protein support skin integrity

slides.title: A client has been hospitalized with a non-life-threatening C-spine neck injury.
text: Question: A client has been hospitalized with a non-life-threatening C-spine neck injury. The interdisciplinary rehabilitation team has worked with the quadriplegic client for 4 months. Which outcome indicates that the team's efforts are effective?
A. Mobility requires multiple assistive devices.
B. Skin is intact, with no evidence of skin impairment.
C. Personal care is performed with help from the family.
D. Constipation now occurs only 3 days a week.
Correct answer: B. Skin is intact, with no evidence of skin impairment.
Topic: GI & Nutrition
notes: Rationale:
Weekly quiz key (one answer):
• Skin is intact, with no evidence of skin impairment.
(This answer was inferred when the master guide was put together; it is not keyed in the original quiz source.)
Study notes from your master guide (not official Galen rationales):
• “Skin is intact, with no evidence of skin impairment.” – Intact skin shows effective pressure injury prevention
Not correct:
• “Mobility requires multiple assistive devices.” – Device use alone does not show complication prevention
• “Personal care is performed with help from the family.” – Family assistance may be appropriate but not the keyed outcome
• “Constipation now occurs only 3 days a week.” – Persistent constipation indicates ongoing issue

text: Question: The nurse is obtaining a focused health history for a client with suspected bacterial meningitis. Which of the following questions should the nurse ask?
A. "Do you live in a crowded residence?"
B. "Have you had any viral infections recently?"
C. "Have you traveled out of the country in the last month?"
D. "When was your last tetanus vaccination?"
Correct answer: A. "Do you live in a crowded residence?"
Topic: Neuro, Eyes & Ortho
notes: Rationale:
Weekly quiz key (one answer):
• "Do you live in a crowded residence?"
(This answer is keyed in the original quiz source.)
Study notes from your master guide (not official Galen rationales):
• “"Do you live in a crowded residence?"” – Crowding increases meningococcal transmission
Not correct:
• “"Have you had any viral infections recently?"” – Less specific for bacterial meningitis
• “"Have you traveled out of the country in the last month?"” – Travel may matter but less specific than crowding
• “"When was your last tetanus vaccination?"” – Tetanus status not a primary meningitis risk

slides.title: A nurse is planning care for a client who has meningitis and is at risk for incr
text: Question: A nurse is planning care for a client who has meningitis and is at risk for increased intracranial pressure (ICP). Which of the following actions should the nurse plan to take?  (Select all that apply.)
A. Administer morphine for the report of neck and generalized pain.
B. Encourage the client to cough frequently
C. Turn off room lights and television.
D. Implement seizure precautions.
E. Monitor for impaired extraocular movements.
F. Perform neurological checks four times a day.
Correct answers: C. Turn off room lights and television.; D. Implement seizure precautions.; E. Monitor for impaired extraocular movements.
Topic: Neuro, Eyes & Ortho
notes: Rationale:
Weekly quiz key (select all):
• Turn off room lights and television.
• Implement seizure precautions.
• Monitor for impaired extraocular movements.
(This answer was inferred when the master guide was put together; it is not keyed in the original quiz source.)
Study notes from your master guide (not official Galen rationales):
• “Turn off room lights and television.” – Reduces stimulation and photophobia
• “Implement seizure precautions.” – Meningitis and increased ICP raise seizure risk
• “Monitor for impaired extraocular movements.” – Cranial nerve changes may signal worsening ICP
Not correct:
• “Administer morphine for the report of neck and generalized pain.” – Opioids may obscure neurologic changes; use cautiously
• “Encourage the client to cough frequently” – Frequent forceful coughing can raise ICP
• “Perform neurological checks four times a day.” – Four daily checks may be too infrequent
✔ Checked against your PowerPoints:
• Unit 5 - Pediatrics, slide 55: “Administer antibiotics, isolate 24 hours, keep area dark and quiet, seizure precautions”
• Unit 10 - Neurological, slide 58: “Continuous neuro assessment”
Your slides support turning off the lights and seizure precautions, and rule out checking neuro status only four times a day; extraocular movements are not named.

text: Question: The nurse is caring for a client recovering from a head injury. The nurse determines that the client needs further education to prevent elevation in ICP if the nurse observes the client doing which of the following? Select all that apply.
A. Bending over to tie the shoes
B. Blowing the nose
C. Exhaling during repositioning
D. Coughing vigorously
E. Isometric exercises
Correct answers: A. Bending over to tie the shoes; B. Blowing the nose; D. Coughing vigorously; E. Isometric exercises
Topic: Neuro, Eyes & Ortho
notes: Rationale:
Weekly quiz key (select all):
• Bending over to tie the shoes
• Blowing the nose
• Coughing vigorously
• Isometric exercises
(This answer was inferred when the master guide was put together; it is not keyed in the original quiz source.)
Study notes from your master guide (not official Galen rationales):
• “Bending over to tie the shoes” – Bending can raise venous and intracranial pressure
• “Blowing the nose” – Nose blowing increases pressure
• “Coughing vigorously” – Vigorous coughing increases ICP
• “Isometric exercises” – Straining during isometrics can raise ICP
Not correct:
• “Exhaling during repositioning” – Exhaling avoids breath-holding and Valsalva

slides.title: What is the goal of therapeutic management for a child diagnosed with ADHD?
text: Question: What is the goal of therapeutic management for a child diagnosed with ADHD?
A. Correct nutritional imbalances.
B. Assess the child for other psychosocial disorders.
C. Administer stimulant medications.
D. Reduce the frequency and intensity of unsocialized behaviors.
Correct answer: D. Reduce the frequency and intensity of unsocialized behaviors.
Topic: Pediatrics
notes: Rationale:
Weekly quiz key (one answer):
• Reduce the frequency and intensity of unsocialized behaviors.
(This answer is keyed in the original quiz source.)
Study notes from your master guide (not official Galen rationales):
• “Reduce the frequency and intensity of unsocialized behaviors.” – Improve functioning and reduce disruptive behaviors
Not correct:
• “Correct nutritional imbalances.” – Nutrition is a consideration but not core behavioral goal
• “Assess the child for other psychosocial disorders.” – Assessment is a means, not therapeutic outcome
• “Administer stimulant medications.” – Medication is a treatment, not goal

slides.title: A nurse is giving a parent information about autism. Which statement made by the
text: Question: A nurse is giving a parent information about autism. Which statement made by the parent indicates understanding of the teaching?
A. Autism can be treated effectively with medication.
B. The onset of autism usually occurs before 3 years of age.
C. Autism is characterized by periods of remission and exacerbation.
D. Children with autism have imitation and gesturing skills.
Correct answer: B. The onset of autism usually occurs before 3 years of age.
Topic: Pediatrics
notes: Rationale:
Weekly quiz key (one answer):
• The onset of autism usually occurs before 3 years of age.
(This answer is keyed in the original quiz source.)
Study notes from your master guide (not official Galen rationales):
• “The onset of autism usually occurs before 3 years of age.” – Signs typically emerge early in development
Not correct:
• “Autism can be treated effectively with medication.” – Medications address associated symptoms, not core autism
• “Autism is characterized by periods of remission and exacerbation.” – Persistent neurodevelopmental condition, not episodic
• “Children with autism have imitation and gesturing skills.” – Imitation and gesturing may be impaired

slides.title: Which are characteristic signs of inflammation? (Select all that apply.)
text: Question: Which are characteristic signs of inflammation? (Select all that apply.)
A. Numbness
B. Heat
C. Edema
D. Paresthesia
E. Erythema
F. Pallor
Correct answers: B. Heat; C. Edema; E. Erythema
Topic: Neuro, Eyes & Ortho
notes: Rationale:
Weekly quiz key (select all):
• Heat
• Edema
• Erythema
(This answer was inferred when the master guide was put together; it is not keyed in the original quiz source.)
Study notes from your master guide (not official Galen rationales):
• “Heat” – Increased local blood flow produces heat
• “Edema” – Increased permeability causes swelling
• “Erythema” – Vasodilation causes redness
Not correct:
• “Numbness” – Sensory change is not a cardinal sign
• “Paresthesia” – Tingling is not a cardinal sign
• “Pallor” – Inflammation typically produces redness rather than pallor
